newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Morris to move some production to Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Morris to move some production to Portugal.

text.p: Philip Morris, which has just won its bid to take over Portuguese tobacco concern Tabaqueira, said on Friday it would move production of its products for sale on the local market to Portugal from the Netherlands and Germany.
"With Marlboro, Chesterfield and L&M we have about 20 percent of the (local) market," the president of Philip Morris Europe, Walter Thoma, told a news conference in Lisbon.
"These products are produced in our factories in Germany and Holland and we'll begin, I hope in January, to fit out the (Portuguese) factory, moving this volume...to produce it here," he said.
"We do not believe this will create job losses in our other factories, nor will it result in the closing of any factory," he said.
The production move will involve a total investment of 7.7 billion escudos over the next three years.
Thoma said the second phase of Morris's investment plan would involve the production in Portugal of products for export.
"In the year 2001 we will probably double current production in this country, taking output to 10 billion cigarettes," he said.

Asked if Tabaqueira was not in danger of creating a monopoly in the domestic tobacco market, Thoma said: "Absolutely not. We and other companies invented this market five years ago with imports and there is a free distribution network."
Philip Morris, who led a consortium with Portugal's Jorge Mello group, on Thursday won the bidding for 65 percent of Tabaqueira. They will pay around 33 billion escudos for the stake.
Under the terms of the privatisation, the consortium must sell off Tabaqueira's wholesale businesses as soon as possible and within a year.
